intent.description: From the doc comment. Omitted when there is none.

Command to clear the prompt. Can be specified like "ctrl-[a-z]" or "ctrl+[a-z]". Defaults to "ctrl+c". Use
`null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

commandSets.description:
Predefined command sets to run on network endpoints with this profile. The "UNIX" set includes the commands
"ifconfig", "netstat -ln", "hostname", and "uname -a". Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property
alone.

customCommands.description:
Additional commands to run on network endpoints with this profile. Commands should be read-only. Use `null`
to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

detectorCommand.description:
CLI command to run to detect a network endpoint of this type. If absent, the profile can be manually
assigned to a network endpoint, but not auto-detected. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property
alone.

detectorErrorPatterns.description:
Patterns matching an error message if a device doesn’t recognize `detectorCommand`. Use `null` to clear.
Omit to leave this property alone.

detectorPatterns.description:
Patterns matching on output of `detectorCommand` to determine whether the device is of this type. Absent if
`detectorCommand` is absent. Never empty. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

name.description: Name of this profile ("HpPrinter", "SamsungTV", etc.). Omit to leave this property alone.

nameDetectorCommand.description:
Command to use to detect the name of a network endpoint of this type. If absent, the name cannot be
detected. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

nameDetectorPatterns.description:
Glob patterns used to extract the device name from the output of `nameDetectorCommand`. The word immediately
after a matched glob pattern is the desired name. If no glob patterns are specified, the first word/token in
the `nameDetectorCommand` output will be used. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

pagePrompt.description:
Case-insensitive glob pattern used to identify a new page banner. Works like `prompt`. If the device doesn’t
generate paginated command output or if paging is like the “more” command, omit this property. Use `null` to
clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

pagePromptResponse.description:
What the Collector should enter in response to an interactive pagination prompt detected via `pagePrompt` in
order to proceed. Required if `pagePrompt` is set. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

prompt.description:
A case-insensitive glob pattern used to identify an interactive console menu prompt. When this pattern
matches the end of the prompt, ignoring any trailing whitespace, the Collector will enter the configured
`promptResponse`. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

promptResponse.description:
What the Collector should enter in response to an interactive console menu prompt matching `prompt` in order
to proceed. Required if `prompt` is set. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

ptyColumnSize.description:
Column size of the output. Defaults to 500. Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property
alone.

ptyType.description:
Device’s terminal type ("xterm-256color", "vt100", etc.). Use `null` to clear. Omit to leave this property
alone.

responseTimeoutSec.description:
Timeout in seconds applied to this profile’s CLI commands run during discovery and collection. Use `null` to
clear. Omit to leave this property alone.

CloudAccount.description: Common fields, with per-type fields beside them: AWS regions and assume-role settings, Azure tenant and subscriptions, GCP projects and regions, IBM accounts and regions, Alkira URL. Secrets and credential ids are never included.

assumeRoleInfos.description: AWS: the assume-role settings. Observed on live AWS accounts.

clientId.description: The Azure application (client) ID, or the GCP client ID. Observed on live AZURE accounts.

discoveredSubscriptionIds.description: Azure subscription IDs found by discovery. Observed on live AZURE accounts.

environment.description: The Azure cloud environment. Observed on live AZURE accounts.

regions.description: AWS: the last test result per region, keyed by region name. Observed on live AWS accounts; each value has error and testInstant.

subscriptionIds.description: The Azure subscription IDs the account covers. Observed on live AZURE accounts.

tenant.description: The Azure tenant ID. Observed on live AZURE accounts.

testResults.description: Azure: the last test result per subscription ID. Observed on live AZURE accounts.

useForwardAccountToAssumeRole.description: AWS: whether Forward's own account is used to assume the role. Observed on live AWS accounts.

CloudAccountConnectivityTest.description: Selected by type. Regions to test as a list, and optional overrides for collector, proxy and timeouts.

CloudAccountCredential.description: Selected by type; no ALKIRA. AWS: username and password, or roleArn. AZURE: clientId, password, tenant. GCP: clientId, clientEmail, privateKeyId, privateKey. IBM_CLOUD: apiKey.

CloudAccountDiscovery.description: A credential to discover accounts with, selected by type; no ALKIRA. The same secret fields as the credential body, plus optional collectorId, proxyServerId, concurrency and timeouts.

error.description: A collection error name; NONE on success.

CloudAccountPatch.description: Selected by type. Every field optional; omitted means unchanged. Credentials cannot be changed here.

awsC2SAccountInfos.description: AWS CAP accounts: replaces the portal-account filter (UpdateAwsAccountRequest.awsC2SAccountInfos, JsonProp). Omit to leave unchanged. Source-only: not observed live.

discoveredProjectIds.description: GCP: replaces the discovered project IDs (UpdateGcpAccountRequest, JsonProp). Omit to leave unchanged.

discoveredSubscriptionIds.description: AZURE: replaces the discovered subscription IDs (UpdateAzureAccountRequest, JsonProp).

projectIds.description: GCP: replaces the project IDs (UpdateGcpAccountRequest.projectIds, JsonProp). Omit to leave unchanged.

subscriptionIds.description: AZURE: replaces the subscription IDs. Presence-aware (JsonProp): omit to leave unchanged. Whether an explicit null clears them is not verified against the source.

CloudConnectivityTest.description: Selected by type. id is a name you choose for the test; the result arrives on the event stream under it. The per-type fields match the create body, with regions as a list rather than a map.

errorMsg.description: Present when this account could not be discovered.

CloudExistingAccountDiscovery.description: Only GCP takes a field, projectIds.

CloudObjectFile.description: A stored file behind a cloud object (StoredFile.java).

CloudObjectInfo.description: One cloud object with the topology it covers (CloudObjectInfo.java). Fields not listed are not modelled.

deviceInfo.description: Present for an object Forward models as a device. Provider-specific; not modelled.

name.description: The object's name, omitted when Forward has none (CloudObjectInfo.java).

vendor.description: Observed on the live server; not a field of CloudObjectInfo.java at the checked-out source.

totalCloudObjects.description: All objects in the snapshot, not only this page.

error.description: A collection error name; NONE on success.

daysOfTheWeek.description:
The days of the week, Sun (0), Mon (1), …, Sat (6), on which the collection schedule is active.
Never empty.

enabled.description: Whether the schedule is currently in effect

endAt.description:
The time of day (in "HH:mm" format) at which a rate-based collection schedule ends. Must be absent if
`times` is specified. Defaults to the end of the day.

periodInSeconds.description:
How many seconds after the start of the most recent collection that the next one should begin. Either
`times` or `periodInSeconds` must be specified—not both. Must be positive.

**Note**: A Collector can only perform one network collection at a time. A scheduled collection will be
delayed if it cannot start on time due to an earlier collection running long.

startAt.description:
The time of day (in "HH:mm" format) at which a rate-based collection schedule begins. Must be absent if
`times` is specified. Defaults to the start of the day (00:00).

timeZone.description:
The time zone used to identify day boundaries and to interpret `times`, `startAt`, and `endAt`. Defaults to
the organization’s preferred time zone.

times.description:
Times of the day (in "HH:mm" format) at which network collections should start. Either `times` or
`periodInSeconds` must be specified—not both. Never empty if present.

endTime.description: Absent while the issue is ongoing.

busyStatus.description: Absent if the network has no Collector assigned

isSet.description: Whether the network has a Collector assigned

canceledBy.description:
The username of the user who canceled this task, if the `status` is CANCELED. Absent if the user account has
been deleted.

canceledById.description: The ID of the user who canceled this task, if the `status` is CANCELED.

createdAt.description: When this entity was created, if known.

createdBy.description:
The ID of the user who created this entity, if known. *Note*: The referenced user account might no longer
exist since an administrator can delete accounts.

createdById.description:
The ID of the user who created this entity, if known. *Note*: The referenced user account might no longer
exist since an administrator can delete accounts.

finishedAt.description: When this task finished. Absent if the task hasn’t finished yet.

networkId.description: The ID of the network this task is associated with

networkName.description: The name of the network this task is associated with

note.description: An optional user-provided note about the task.

startedAt.description: When this task started. Absent if the task hasn’t started yet.

status.description: The current status of the task.

CollectorTaskId.description: A collector task ID. E followed by a number for an ephemeral task, P for a persistent one.

CollectorWithAuthKey.description: A newly created collector account, plus the one-time key its installer needs. The key is returned only from creation -- it cannot be fetched again afterwards.

authorizationKey.description: Opaque install key for the collector's fwd.properties/installer. V2 format is literally `username:password`; V3 is a base64-encoded protobuf that also carries the app server URL.

CollectorWithStatus.description: The collector's own fields sit flat beside its status. Empty when no collector is bound to the network.

commands.description: The command text, one command per line.

CommitResult.description: The outcome of a commit, or the report from a dry run.

newErrors.description: Errors the change would introduce. Non-empty means do not commit.

uses.description: Existing queries that depend on the ones being changed.

CommittedChangeSet.description: A commit with the change set's device changes as of that commit, flattened together.

ConfigValue.description: A single property and its value, keyed by the property name in lower case. Read it with `forward_sdk.config_value`, which returns the value whatever the key.

ConfigValues.description: Property name to value, one entry per property.

invalidSource.description: True when the source no longer resolves to anything in the snapshot.

ConnectivityDetailsValue.description: headers describes one packet-header region that has this connectivity; several values together cover every case. sampleQuery is a concrete example packet from that region, when one applies.

ConnectivityTestResult.description: A SourceConnectivityResult plus which source it is for.

CoveredTopology.description: A minimal topology sketch scoped to one zone's devices.

name.description: Absent for an inferred host.

cloudAccounts.description:
Names of the cloud accounts
[AWS](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/application/sources/configure-collection/cloud/aws-setup/),
[GCP](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/application/sources/configure-collection/cloud/gcp-setup/), or
[Azure](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/application/sources/configure-collection/cloud/azure-setup/) to
include. Can be omitted or empty if `devices` or `vcenters` is nonempty.

devices.description:
Names of the [classic devices](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/api/classic-devices/) to include. Can be omitted or
empty if `cloudAccounts` or `vcenters` is nonempty.

omissions.description: What to omit (not copy) from the parent network

retentionDays.description:
Number of days of inactivity after which the Workspace network will be deleted. If omitted, the value
defaults to 7. If specified as null, this network will be considered permanent.

vcenters.description:
Names of the
[vCenters](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/application/sources/configure-collection/vmware-account/#adding-a-vcenter-source)
to include. Can be omitted or empty if `devices` or `cloudAccounts` is nonempty.

CurrentUser.description: The calling user. Note the account is nested under `user`; the roles sit beside it rather than inside it.

CurrentUserRoles.description: The roles the calling user holds. `org` applies across the organization; `network` maps a network id to the role held on it. Integrations read both to decide whether a login may write to the shared query library.

org.description: Usually a list, but observed as a bare string, so consumers coerce.

CustomCveStatus.description:
A vulnerability status a rule can assign to the devices it matches, overriding the automatically computed status:
`VULNERABLE` marks the devices as affected by the CVE, and `NOT_VULNERABLE` marks them as unaffected.

name.description:
A concise name for the OID’s value. Used in the name of the file the Collector creates when it retrieves the
OID’s value from a device. Can contain only letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens.

oid.description:
A numeric object identifier (OID) from the Management Information Base (MIB) for the Simple Network
Management Protocol (SNMP).

analyses.description: The custom vulnerability analyses defined for the CVE.

cveId.description: The ID of the CVE this analysis applies to.

os.description: The OS this analysis applies to.

rules.description: The analysis rules, applied first to last.

CveAnalysis.description:
A custom vulnerability analysis for one CVE and OS: an ordered list of rules that override the automatically computed
vulnerability status of the devices they match. For each device, the first rule that the device matches determines
its status. `rules` is empty when no analysis has been defined for the CVE and OS.

rules.description:
The analysis rules, applied first to last. Must contain between 1 and 4 rules. For each device, the first rule
that the device matches determines its custom vulnerability status.

CveAnalysisRule.description:
A single analysis rule: device criteria plus the attributes to apply to the devices they match. A device matches a
rule only if it satisfies every criterion the rule specifies (`deviceGlobs`, `tags`, `locationIds`, `osVersions`,
`models`); each criterion in turn matches a device that satisfies any one of its values. At least one criterion must
be specified.

comment.description: A longer explanation of why this rule was added.
examples: Confirmed patched by the network team on 2024-11-02.

deviceGlobs.description:
Glob patterns matched against device names. A device matches this criterion if its name matches any of these
patterns, ignoring case.

label.description: A short label summarizing the effect of this rule, shown alongside the devices it matches.

locationIds.description:
The `id`s of [Network Locations](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/api/network-locations/). A device matches this
criterion if it is in any of these locations.

models.description: A device matches this criterion if it is any of these models.

osVersions.description: A device matches this criterion if it runs any of these OS versions.

status.description:
The status to assign to devices this rule matches. Omit to apply the label and comment without changing the
matched device’s computed status.

tags.description: A device matches this criterion if it carries any of these tags.

examples:
An issue is present in Apache ZooKeeper 1.0.0 to 3.4.13 and 3.5.0-alpha to 3.5.4-beta. ZooKeeper’s getACL()
command…

hasCisaKevEntry.description:
Whether CISA’s [KEV Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) mentions a known
exploit for this CVE.

id.description:
The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures ([CVE](https://www.cve.org)) ID assigned to this vulnerability in
the National Vulnerability Database ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov)).

weaknesses.description:
Common Weakness Enumeration ([CWE](https://cwe.mitre.org/about/new_to_cwe.html)) IDs associated with this
CVE.

advisoryMentionsExploit.description: Whether the vendor advisory at `url` says there’s a known exploit. Included only if true.

configAnalysis.description:
Present and can be any allowed value if `configDependent` is true. Absent if `configDependent` is false.
Can be either "UNSUPPORTED" or absent if `configDependent` is absent (unknown).

configDependent.description: Whether this vulnerability depends on a device’s configuration for this OS. Absent if unknown.

publishDate.description: Publication date of the information at `url` if known.

severity.description:
Severity based on one of this vulnerability’s CVSS scores according to the [Qualitative Severity
Ratings](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln-metrics/cvss#:~:text=Qualitative%20Severity%20Ratings) table. The priority
order of scores is `v4Score`, then `v3Score`, then `v2Score`. "NONE" if no CVSS score is available for this
vulnerability.

url.description:
URL of this vulnerability’s vendor advisory, if available, or else the URL of the best source of information
about the vulnerability that’s currently available.

v2Score.description:
Score assigned by the Common Vulnerability Scoring System ([CVSS](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln-metrics/cvss))
v2.0 standard.

v3Score.description:
Score assigned by the Common Vulnerability Scoring System ([CVSS](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln-metrics/cvss))
v3.x standard.

v4Score.description:
Score assigned by the Common Vulnerability Scoring System
([CVSS](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)) v4.0 standard.

deviceCount.description:
Total number of devices in the network that are running an affected version of this OS and thus are
potentially affected by this CVE.

locationIds.description: The IDs of the locations of the devices in the network that are potentially affected by this CVE.

osVersions.description: The OS versions of the devices in the network that are potentially affected by this CVE.

resultCounts.description:
The number of devices in the network that are potentially affected by this CVE broken down by detection
result. These counts add up to `deviceCount`.

tags.description:
Tags associated with any devices in the network that are potentially affected by this CVE. Absent if the
devices have no tags.

examples: Back in February we were contacted by Hanno Böck who had discovered an issue with how certain...

devices.description:
Devices in the network that are running an affected version of this OS and thus are potentially affected by
this CVE. A detection result is included for each device. Relevant lines of device configuration are
included for each device as well when possible.

Dashboard.description: type DEFAULT for the fixed dashboards Forward ships, COMPOSED for yours.

DashboardDisplaySettings.description: Every field optional; a never-customised dashboard reads as an empty object.

DashboardPatch.description: Omitted means unchanged. A present layout replaces the whole layout.

DashboardWidget.description: Selected by type. A ROW has a title and children, which must not be rows. A PANEL has a panelId such as NQE_PANEL_7, DEFINED_3 or CUSTOM_SCORECARD_2; an NQE panel may also carry an override and a server-assigned id that identifies the embedding across saves.

id.description: Server-assigned per embedding; echo it to keep the embedding

override.description: displayName, queryParams, or a config override; at least one.

baseUrl.description:
The scheme, host, and optional port of the service to fetch from, with no trailing slash. Each endpoint’s
`path` is appended to it.

collect.description: Whether to collect from this data connector. Absent if it has never been set, which means true.

collectorId.description:
The `id` of the Collector that collects from this data connector. Absent if Forward picks an online Collector
that supports it.

credentialId.description:
The `id` of an HttpCredential to authenticate with. Absent if the service accepts unauthenticated
requests.

disableSslValidation.description:
Whether to skip TLS validation. Absent unless `baseUrl` uses the https scheme and validation is
disabled.

endpoints.description:
The HTTP GET requests issued on every collection, each one relative to `baseUrl`. Never empty. Each
endpoint’s response is stored under its own name in the Snapshot. An endpoint whose dataset arrives in pages
has a `paginationModel`.

extraHeaders.description:
HTTP headers sent with every request to this service. Absent if no extra headers are
configured.

name.description:
A name that’s unique (ignoring case) among all of the network’s collection source names. It identifies
this connector in the NQE data model. May consist of letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores.

proxyServerId.description:
The `id` of a proxy server to route requests through. Absent if the Collector reaches the service
directly.

status.description:
How the most recent collection from this connector went. Absent unless `?with=status` is used, and absent then
too if the network has no processed Snapshot or that Snapshot didn’t collect this connector.

error.description:
What went wrong collecting from this connector. Absent if collection succeeded. "NONE" never
occurs.

testResult.description:
The outcome of the most recent connectivity test of this connector. Absent if it has never been tested, or if
the connector changed in a way that invalidated the result. When listing or getting connectors, also absent
unless `?with=testResult` is used.

endedAt.description: When Forward received the test result, or stopped waiting for one.

error.description:
What went wrong during the test. Absent if every endpoint responded successfully. "NONE" never
occurs.

errorDesc.description: A human-readable explanation of `error`. Absent if the test succeeded.

startedAt.description: When the Collector began the test.

snapshotId.description:
The network’s latest processed Snapshot, which is the one every `status` describes. Absent unless `?with=status`
is used, and absent then too if the network has no processed Snapshot.

DataFileCreateRequest.description: The JSON part named request of addDataFile (DataFileCreateRequest.java).

headers.description: Column names, for a CSV with no header row only. No duplicates.

name.description: Data file name. Forward lower-cases it. Must be unique (case-insensitively) in the org.

nqeName.description: Name queries use for the file (network.extensions.<nqeName>). Defaults to the name without its extension (for STIG, the name).

content.description: For CSV, the first rows of the file; otherwise the whole content.

dataFormat.description: JSON, CSV or TEXT. Omitted when no format was recognised.

errors.description: Non-empty means Forward would not accept the file as this type.

schema.description: The inferred NQE type, in the InlinedType form GET /api/nqe/schema uses. Omitted when nothing was inferred.

contentMd5Hex.description: MD5 of the stored content. Set on GET /data-files only (source DataFileInfo doc).

isEmpty.description: true for a placeholder imported from a snapshot, which cannot be downloaded. Omitted when false.

isIncludedInAllNetworks.description: true only for the STIG policy file. Omitted otherwise.

networkIds.description: Networks the file is attached to. Omitted when none.

description.description: New description. An explicit null clears it.

name.description: New name (lower-cased). Refused if a collection source in an attached network already uses it.

nqeName.description: New NQE name. Must not be blank; null is refused.

columnName.description: The name of a column to filter on.

value.description: A value (in its string representation) to match on.

collectionError.description:
Absent if there was no collection error. "NONE" never occurs and will soon be removed from the
value list.

displayName.description:
The device’s common name, if different from `"name"`. Absent for most network devices. For a cloud device,
this is the name shown in the cloud provider’s console.

locationId.description:
The `id` of the device’s assigned Location (see
[Network Locations](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/api/network-locations/)). Present only if specifically requested.
Defaults to "default" (the Unassigned location).

managementIps.description: Absent if no management IP addresses are known.

model.description: Absent if the device model name is unknown.

[classic device](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/api/classic-devices/) name. For a virtual context, this is the
classic device name plus context name. For a cloud device, this is a globally unique identifier assigned by the
cloud provider.

osVersion.description: Absent if the OS version is unknown.

processingError.description: Absent if there was no processing error.

sourceName.description:
Name of this device’s collection source (such as a
[classic device](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/api/classic-devices/)), if different from `"name"`. Absent for most
network devices. For a cloud device, this is the cloud setup ID.

tags.description: Tags assigned to the device. Present only if specifically requested.

deviceGlobs.description: Device-name patterns (wildcards and character classes). Omitted when empty.

deviceNames.description: Lowercased device names. Omitted when empty.

name.description: Unique (ignoring case) within the org.

devicesCount.description: Devices in the org the label matches.

DeviceAccessLabelInfo.description: A device access label with the counts the list route adds.

DeviceAccessLabelNames.description: Device access label ID to name.

deviceNames.description: Replaces the device names when present. Null or empty clears them.

forwardingOutcome.description:
Specifies the traffic forwarding outcome along a path.
*DELIVERED*: Traffic was delivered to destination IP’s discovered location(s).
*DELIVERED_TO_INCORRECT_LOCATION*: Traffic was delivered out of some edge ports. However, traffic did not
reach the expected delivery locations based on destination IP’s discovered locations. One scenario where
this occurs is when a device in the middle of the actual path from source IP to destination IP is not
configured for collection in the Forward platform. For example, suppose the actual device path is A -> B ->
C, and only devices A and C are part of the snapshot in the Forward platform. In this case, the path would
show traffic exiting device A at some edge port, but since destination IP is discovered to reside at device
C, traffic is delivered to an incorrect location.
*BLACKHOLE*: Traffic was implicitly dropped at the last hop, since the device had no matching rule. For
example, if a router does not have a default route, traffic to any IP that is not in the routing table gets
blackholed.
*DROPPED*: Traffic was explicitly dropped at the last hop, e.g. by a null route.
*INADMISSIBLE*: Traffic was not admitted into the network. The first hop interface does not accept the
traffic, e.g. incoming traffic had a vlan tag 10 while the ingress interface is an access interface that
only permits traffic with vlan tag 20.
*UNREACHABLE*: ARP/NDP resolution failed along the path resulting in traffic not getting delivered to the
intended destination.
*LOOP*: Traffic entered a forwarding loop.

securityOutcome.description:
Specifies whether traffic is denied by ACL rules at any hop along the path.
*PERMITTED*: All ACLs along the path permitted traffic to flow through.
*DENIED*: Traffic was dropped by ACLs at some hop along the path. Note that the ACL drop may not always
occur at the last hop since search results are computed in permit all mode.

backfilledFrom.description: the collection instant from which the device was backfilled

behaviors.description:
Specifies the forwarding behaviors experienced by traffic at the device.
*L2*: Forwarded at layer 2.
*L3*: Routed at layer 3.
*NAT*: NAT transformations applied.
*PBR*: Forwarded using Policy-Based Routing.
*ACL_PERMIT*: ACLs were applied to traffic at the device and the traffic was permitted.
*ACL_DENY*: ACLs were applied to traffic at the device and the traffic was dropped.

devices, this is the name configured in the cloud provider’s console.

intent.description:
Specifies the intent for the search. Default PREFER_DELIVERED.
*PREFER_VIOLATIONS*: Prefer paths that result in the traffic not getting delivered, e.g. drops, blackholes,
loops. An example usage is while trying to evaluate if the specified traffic always gets delivered to the
destination along all path choices.
*PREFER_DELIVERED*: Prefer paths that result in the traffic getting delivered. An example usage is while
trying to evaluate if traffic gets delivered to the destination along any path choice.
*VIOLATIONS_ONLY*: Search for paths where traffic is not delivered to the destination.

maxCandidates.description:
the limit on the number of search results computed, before applying any ranking criteria. Permitted range =
1 to 10,000. Default 5,000.

maxOverallSeconds.description:
the overall timeout duration. Permitted range = 1 to 7,200. Default equal to the timeout duration for a
single query.

maxResults.description:
the limit on the number of search results returned by the API. First, the platform computes up to
maxCandidates results that match the search criteria. Then they are sorted by various ranking criteria. A
key ranking factor is path length, preferring longer paths (greatest reach) in the network over shorter
ones. Finally, the API limits the number of returned search results to maxResults. Permitted range = 1 to
maxCandidates. Default 1.

maxReturnPathResults.description:
the limit on the number of return path search results. Permitted range = 0 to 10,000. Default 0. Multicast
(*, G) and (S, G) queries will always return 0 return path results regardless of this value.

maxSeconds.description: the timeout duration per search query. Permitted range = 1 to 300. Default 30.

queries.description:
The path search queries to evaluate. Up to 20,000 queries are permitted, but ~1,000 per request is recommended
to maximize throughput.

ack.description: the ACK (acknowledgment) bit (0 or 1). Implies ipProto = 6.

appId.description:
the L7 app-id or "unidentified" to exclude paths that traverse firewall policies with app-id matches. If the
system doesn't recognize the provided value, it handles the value the same as "unidentified" and includes
the value in the `unrecognizedValues` response field. The applications that are recognized by the model can
be obtained using GET /api/l7-applications.

domain.description:

which implies HTTP/HTTPS over TCP/UDP, this field matches on domain regardless of application protocol (e.g.,
ICMP to a domain). Prefix wildcards are supported for subdomains and suffix wildcards for top-level domains.
Cannot be specified together with `url`.

dstIp.description:
the destination IP address or subnet of packets entering the network. For multicast (*, G) paths, set dstIp
= G (multicast group address).

dstPort.description: the L4 destination port, like "80" or a range "8080-8088"

fin.description: the FIN (finish) bit (0 or 1). Implies ipProto = 6.

from.description:

packet header only, else, the srcIp will be resolved to specific location(s) and used as the source in the
path search. Either the source device or srcIp must be specified.

psh.description: the PSH (push) bit (0 or 1). Implies ipProto = 6.

rst.description: the RST (reset) bit (0 or 1). Implies ipProto = 6.

srcIp.description:

(multicast group address).

srcPort.description: the L4 source port, like "80" or a range "8080-8088"

syn.description: the SYN (synchronize) bit (0 or 1). Implies ipProto = 6.

urg.description: the URG (urgent) bit (0 or 1). Implies ipProto = 6.

url.description:
the L7 URL that traffic of interest is trying to access. Prefix wildcards are supported for subdomains.
Suffix wildcards are supported for top-level domains and URL paths. See [Path Analysis with Layer 7
URL](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/application/search/path-analysis/layer7-url/) for more policy patterns supported
in the model.

userGroupId.description:
the L7 user-group-id. If the system doesn't recognize the provided value, the search returns 0 results as
there are no paths that traverse firewall policies with that user-group-id match, and the value is included
in the `unrecognizedValues` response field. See [Path Analysis with Layer 7
User-Group](https://docs.fwd.app/latest/application/search/path-analysis/layer7-ugroup/) for more info.

userId.description:
the L7 user-id or "unidentified" to exclude paths that traverse firewall policies with user-id matches. If
the system doesn't recognize the provided value, it handles the value the same as "unidentified" and
includes the value in the `unrecognizedValues` response field. See [Path Analysis with Layer 7

dstIpLocationType.description:
Specifies the location discovery method for destination IP.
The enum values are ordered from most precise to least precise discovery method.
*INTERFACE*: The IP is a configured IP address of one or more device interfaces.
*HOST*: The IP corresponds to discovered host(s).
*DNAT*: The IP gets DNAT'd in the network. The IP may either correspond directly to a VIP on a load balancer
or a DNAT'd IP on other devices such as routers. This discovery method is only used to locate destination IP
addresses. DNAT’d IP addresses are recursively resolved to determine where traffic to a given destination IP
must be delivered in the network.
*CO_LOCATED*: The IP is configured on a gateway device as a /32 or /128 route whose next hop is a known
host.
*INTERFACE_ATTACHED_SUBNET*: The IP falls within the attached subnet of L3 interface(s).
*INTERNET*: The IP is in the public internet and was located at the network's Internet Node. This discovery
method is only applicable when an Internet Node is configured in the network.
*ROUTE*: The IP was located based on injected routes in the network.
*MULTICAST*: The IP is a multicast group address.

queryUrl.description: A Forward application URL at which this path search can be explored or refined interactively

srcIpLocationType.description:
Specifies the location discovery method for source IP.
The enum values are ordered from most precise to least precise discovery method.
*INTERFACE*: The IP is a configured IP address of one or more device interfaces.
*HOST*: The IP corresponds to discovered host(s).
*SNAT* : The IP is used as the post-translated IP of a Source NAT function in the network and is assumed to
be located on the gateway device(s) performing this translation.
*CO_LOCATED*: The IP is configured on a gateway device as a /32 or /128 route whose next hop is a known
host.
*INTERFACE_ATTACHED_SUBNET*: The IP falls within the attached subnet of L3 interface(s).
*INTERNET*: The IP is in the public internet and was located at the network's Internet Node. This discovery
method is only applicable when an Internet Node is configured in the network.
*ROUTE*: The IP was located based on injected routes in the network.
*MULTICAST*: The IP is a multicast group address. This discovery method is used to locate the rendezvous
points of the multicast group and use their IP addresses as IP source.

Number of ways in which traffic matching the search criteria is forwarded in the network. Multiple ECMP path
choices for traffic lead to separate results. In addition, depending on the scope of query terms, there
might be multiple results along a single path. For example a search without IP protocol or destination port
restrictions can result in multiple results along a single device path if there are different ACLs that
permit or deny traffic to different destination ports.

requested number of hits were found, or the request timed out.
*EXACT*: There are exactly this many hits.
